content.body:
The FlaK 36 was actually developed during the interwar years by German engineers working in Sweden, who managed to produce probably the most famous and effective gun system in the war. It was originally designed as an anti-aircraft gun, but Spanish experience showed its amazing utility against tanks as well.
Fortunately for Rommel, the armor-piercing shells needed were already distributed to FlaK units for emergency use when he was confronted by a breakout of British Matilda IIs at Arras. A scratch force of FlaK 36s defeated them at point-blank range. The 88 later came to be so feared that some British crews abandoned their tanks after even a near miss by an 88, knowing that the remarkable gun and its crews rarely missed a second time. It remained a potent gun throughout WW2. Even at the end, the 88 could penetrate the front of any tank in the British or American inventory at most ranges.
In the hands of a skilled operator the FlaK 36 can be devastating. It is able to move on its own by crew pushing it, but this is really only useful for emergencies and to relocate the gun around obstacles. You need to get a SdKfz 7 to pull this gun to a clear vantage point with long sightlines. As they are most-favored targets for Allied strafing, 88s should always deploy under trees or bushes. Like the Bofors, it is useful to place it on a hill, below the crest to prevent skylining. If you are under fire, undeploy and roll down the hill until you are safe.
Because of your ability to dominate an entire battlefield, you are a prime target for EVERYONE: every tank, plane, gun, and grunt will cheerfully use everything they have got to get rid of you. It is sometimes a good idea to have a 232 or other AFV nearby with a rapid-fire gun to deal with aircraft and/or infantry (although their gray paint will highlight your location). If it is a big enough vehicle, have it park in front of you - your gun is high enough to fire over almost anything, and their chassis will protect you from the spatter of long-range MG fire.
The FlaK 36 commander has a cross hair and rangefinder so you should be able to dial in the ranges to a number of landmarks and be ready to re-set your sights to the proper range. With the range dialed properly in, the gun is incredibly accurate. First-shot hits at 2,000 m are the norm with a skilled user, and even a novice can easily kill enemy tanks at 1,500 m. Some vehicles like the B1 or the Matilda may prove a bit tougher to crack, but even they rarely stand a chance at 1,000 m or less.
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Commander 2 Gunner
